subject: Post-demo: Xenith inference readiness & MAP items
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Marie Gomez <marie@xenith.ai>, David Perez <david.perez@xenith.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Nov 2028 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo: Xenith inference readiness & MAP items

Hi Marie / David—

Thanks again for the demo earlier — great conversation. This thread is a short recap of the performance checkpoints we discussed and the next-step MAP so your engineering and infra teams have a single reference. I attached the snapshot you requested (xenith-metrics-snapshot.csv) and our preliminary SLO checklist (redwood-slo-checklist.pdf).

Key performance targets you confirmed during the call:
- Latency: 95th percentile <= 220ms for request size ~512 tokens (non-streaming).
- Streaming: token-forward latency <= 80ms p95 (real-time UI experience).
- Throughput: baseline 350 requests/minute sustained (~6 RPS) with burst to 1500 requests/minute (~25 RPS).
- Concurrency: support 60 concurrent open streams per region with graceful degradation beyond 100.

Open infra/clarity items for Redwood ops to validate:
1) Payload distribution: we need a 48-hour sample of production request size distribution (you committed to share by Thu).
2) Auth & region routing: confirm whether EU traffic routes to a dedicated EU region or will go to us-west fallback.
3) Expected KPIs for cold-start vs warmed model: define acceptable p95 delta for first token after an idle period.

Immediate MAP (assignments + due dates):
- Xenith: share 48h request sample + safety/PII notes (action: Marie) — due: 2028-11-30.
- Redwood (Eng - Karthik): validate model variant selection & expected 95th latency under our streaming engine — due: 2028-12-04.
- Redwood (Sales - Ben): draft initial draft T-shirt pricing for Dedicated pool and estimated monthly commit for target throughput — due: 2028-12-01.
- Joint: schedule a 60m ops sync to review real traces and run a quick pilot checklist (Ben/Soojin to propose times) — target week of 2028-12-04.

Please reply on-thread if any of the targets above should be adjusted. If everything looks right I'll kick off the pilot ops ticket and loop in our SRE for a capacity validation run.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
--
Attachments: xenith-metrics-snapshot.csv (CSV, 1.2MB), redwood-slo-checklist.pdf (PDF, 420KB)
From: Marie Gomez <marie@xenith.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: David Perez <david.perez@xenith.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Nov 2028 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Xenith inference readiness & MAP items

Thanks Vivek — appreciate the tidy summary. A few clarifications from our side after sharing the metrics snapshot: we confirmed the sample is from production (last 48h) and includes a mix of short user prompts (median ~40 tokens) and long-form generation spikes (~1,200 tokens) when batch jobs run.

Quick clarifications:
- The 220ms p95 target is for our interactive product flows only. For the batch jobs (long-form generation) we expect higher latency and are prepared to route those to a lower-cost Dedicated tier.
- For streaming, our UX team wants first-token-to-display under 60ms p95 if possible; we understand that depends on model variant and kernel selection.
- Concurrency: the 60 concurrent streams is our steady-state target; during product launches we'd need to support short bursts to 220 concurrent streams for up to 15 minutes.

We can share sanitized request traces by end of day Thu (2028-11-30). Also attaching a short doc with our security constraints and regional restrictions (will share via Drive link in follow-up).

From an acceptance standpoint — our internal decision criteria (to greenlight a pilot):
1) Redwood demonstrates < 250ms p95 non-streaming for 512-token simulations in our config.
2) Streaming path achieves <= 80ms p95 per token for 95% of interactive traffic (with a fallback for spikes).
3) Clear rollback/fallback plan to a smaller model variant with negligible feature loss.

We expect to make a pilot go/no-go decision after the ops sync; will bring infra owners.

– Marie
VP, Platform Engineering, Xenith AI
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marie Gomez <marie@xenith.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Nov 2028 07:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Xenith inference readiness & MAP items

Marie — quick pricing note to align expectations before the ops sync:
- Preliminary estimate (monthly steady-state commit to cover baseline throughput + on-demand bursting): $23k/month for Dedicated pool sized to 6 RPS sustained with autoscaling headroom.
- Streaming add-on (low-latency path with token-forward guarantees) estimated at +30% on top of base.
- Pilot discount available; I will include a 6-week evaluation credit in the proposal.

I'll circulate a short pricing doc and proposed SOW draft by Friday (2028-12-01). We can carve options for routing batch jobs to cheaper capacity as Marie suggested.

Ben
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Marie Gomez <marie@xenith.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Nov 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Xenith inference readiness & MAP items

Marie / team —

Thanks for the trace commitment — that will let Karthik and our serving team run a focused validation with a matched model variant. A couple of operational commitments from Redwood to help Xenith evaluate quickly:
- Validation run plan: Karthik will run two simulations this week against your sample — (A) interactive-case (512 token median) and (B) mixed-load batch spike (1200 tokens). We will provide p50/p95/p99 latency tables, memory utilization, and KV cache hit-rate.
- Canary plan: if results align, we'll propose a canary across a small subset of your traffic (1% -> 5% -> 20%) with automatic rollback thresholds if p95 exceeds agreed SLOs for two consecutive 5-minute windows.
- Fallback: model-variant downgrade policy (downgrade to quantized variant preserving same API surface) with feature gates for streaming.

Next steps for schedule: Ben — can you propose 3 time slots for the 60m ops sync during the week of Dec 4? Marie — once we have the trace, engineering will start the sim run and post the first report in this thread (target 2028-12-04).

Soojin Lee
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
